comparison: Both strongly support the core finding of spatial segregation between commensal and pathogenic bacteria (C1, C2, C15, C24, C28, C31-C33). OpenEval provides detailed methodological validation citing videos and quantitative blockage ratios, while peer reviewers describe this as 'compelling evidence' and 'a novel mechanism.' Both evaluations are fully aligned with SUPPORTED status.

Perfect claim overlap (C37-C42) regarding rapid kinetics and dose-response. Both support the findings. OpenEval notes the 15-30 min timing logically supports transcription/translation independence (C41) as an inference. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly acknowledges 'This muscle contraction-related blocking happens early after infection (15mins).' Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Strong overlap on genetic requirements (C43, C45, C5, C6, C52-C53) for TrpA1 and Dh31. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval notes bacterial persistence in mutants (C44) provides indirect evidence for killing in controls with caveats about alternative explanations. Peer reviewers describe genetic evidence as 'compelling' without raising these caveats. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address ROS mechanism (C54-C56). OpenEval includes additional claims about Duox RNAi (C4, C51) not explicitly mentioned in peer result. Both support ROS as critical signal. OpenEval notes lack of direct in vivo ROS measurement as limitation. Peer reviewers (R1, R3) acknowledge ROS/Duox mechanism without questioning evidence quality. Both SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on Duox requirement (C4, C51). OpenEval R4 focuses on ROS signaling role, while Peer R3 addresses broader genetic requirements including TrpA1/Dh31. Both support the Duox/ROS mechanism as part of the pathway. Complementary rather than directly comparable evaluations.

Perfect claim overlap (C7, C8, C46-C50) on hCGRP experiments and conservation. Both support findings. OpenEval notes evolutionary conservation claim (C8) would benefit from additional cross-species validation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept conservation evidence without detailed critique, suggesting acceptance of hCGRP functional complementation as sufficient. Both SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on bacterial elimination evidence (C59-C61, C86). OpenEval R6 focuses on time-lapse imaging and CFU data showing bacterial killing. Peer R2 addresses broader claims about AMP-mediated clearance and IMD pathway role (C3, C9, C14, C91, C96). Both support bacterial elimination but emphasize different aspects of evidence. Both SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on survival and bacterial proliferation in mutants (C62, C67, C72). OpenEval includes additional mechanistic claims (C63, C65-C66, C68-C71) about uniform initial loads and DTT experiments. Peer R7 emphasizes broader significance claims (C10-C13, C102, C121) about importance of compartmentalization. Both strongly support that blockage is essential for survival. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C73-C78) on cellular localization of TrpA1/Dh31/Pros markers. Both support the anatomical characterization. OpenEval notes decreased Dh31 during blockage (C78) suggests secretion without direct measurement. Peer Reviewer 2 acknowledges 'previously understudied structure' characterization. Both SUPPORTED with implicit acceptance of evidence quality.

Perfect claim overlap (C79-C85) on TARM muscle anatomy and valve hypothesis. Both support findings. OpenEval notes valve closure not directly demonstrated. Peer reviewers accept anatomical evidence and functional interpretation, with Reviewer 2 highlighting TARM as 'previously understudied structure' playing 'crucial role.' Both SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on IMD pathway independence from blockage (C10, C88, C95). OpenEval R10 includes broader claims about multiple IMD mutants and AMP requirement (C89-C92, C96). Peer R6 emphasizes separation of blockage from elimination mechanisms. Both support that IMD/AMPs are dispensable for blockage but required for elimination. Both SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on AMP-mediated elimination (C9, C91, C96). OpenEval R10 provides detailed genetic evidence with multiple IMD pathway mutants. Peer R2 addresses broader bacterial elimination claims including CFU data. Both support AMPs eliminate trapped bacteria. Complementary evaluations, both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C93-C94) on spatial correlation between bacterial localization and AMP expression. Both support findings from reporter gene imaging. OpenEval notes temporal dynamics could be better characterized. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as supporting regional immune response model. Both SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on reinterpretation of previous literature (C97-C98). OpenEval R18 addresses unifying mechanism inference as reasonable but speculative. Peer R14 includes additional reinterpretation claims (C99-C101, C103). OpenEval marks R18 as SUPPORTED while R19 (covering C99-C101, C103) is UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers accept reinterpretation framework as SUPPORTED without distinguishing speculation levels.

Strong overlap on reinterpretation of Ramond et al. 2021 findings (C99-C101, C103). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting alternative interpretation is plausible but speculative without direct testing. Peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting reinterpretation through acknowledgment of 'substantially advances understanding.' Key disagreement: OpenEval more cautious about speculative reinterpretations.

Partial overlap on importance of compartmentalization for survival (C102, C121). OpenEval R20 focuses specifically on these claims with survival data support. Peer R7 includes broader context (C11-C13, C62, C67, C72) about bacterial proliferation and larval death. Both strongly support this key conclusion. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C122-C125) on regionalized immunity model integrating previous literature. Both support the interpretation. OpenEval notes direct measurement of regional responses in current experiments would strengthen conclusion. Peer R13 accepts model but notes as weakness that 'mechanism allowing discrimination between commensal and pathogenic bacteria remains unclear.' Both SUPPORTED with caveats.

Strong overlap on larval-adult comparison (C108-C110). OpenEval includes C130 on mobility differences. Both support the comparative interpretation. OpenEval notes developmental difference in outcomes (C109) is inference-based. Peer reviewers implicitly accept comparison through acknowledgment of mechanism as 'novel' without challenging larval-adult distinction. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong overlap on temporal coordination model (C115-C120). OpenEval R25 includes additional claims (C114) about synthesis. Both support the two-phase mechanism interpretation. OpenEval notes direct kinetic measurements of AMP production would strengthen conclusion. Peer reviewers accept temporal coordination concept through acknowledgment of mechanism as 'fundamentally important.' Both SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on larval-adult strategy comparison (C130). OpenEval R26 addresses broader ecological/evolutionary context (C126-C131) marked as SUPPORTED but speculative. Peer R15 implicitly accepts through acknowledgment of conservation aspects. Both support adaptive significance interpretations as reasonable inferences.

Minimal overlap on ROS dual role (C57). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting dual role (bactericidal and signaling) is plausible but not experimentally separated. Peer R4 addresses ROS signaling role (C54-C56) as SUPPORTED without explicitly discussing dual role speculation. OpenEval more cautious about mechanistic speculation.

Minimal overlap on evolutionary conservation claim (C8). OpenEval R28 marks as UNCERTAIN, noting conservation is at molecular level (CGRP/Dh31 homology) rather than mechanistic level of immune strategy, calling claim overstated. Peer R5 marks as SUPPORTED, accepting hCGRP functional complementation as sufficient evidence. Key disagreement on interpretation scope.

OpenEval addresses reversibility of blockage (C27, C34) with video and anatomical evidence, marked SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found explicitly addressing these claims, though reversibility is implicit in accepted mechanism.

OpenEval addresses non-feeding rates and distinction from feeding cessation (C29-C30), marked SUPPORTED with note that direct food intake measurement would strengthen conclusion. No corresponding peer review evaluation found explicitly addressing these control experiments.

OpenEval addresses Uracil negative result (C58), marked SUPPORTED but with limited interpretation due to single concentration tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this negative control experiment.

OpenEval addresses intestinal contractions in Dh31 mutants (C64) as control for gut motility, marked SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found explicitly addressing this control, though general mechanism is accepted by peers.
OpenEval addresses background knowledge claims (C16-C23) from literature, marked SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate background claims separately, focusing on novel findings.
OpenEval addresses bacterial cell wall composition background (C87), marked SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background information claim.

OpenEval addresses anatomical observations and pylorus analogy (C104-C107), marked SUPPORTED with note that 'valve' remains descriptive rather than mechanistically defined. No separate peer evaluation found, though anatomical findings are implicitly accepted in R8-R9.

OpenEval addresses valve dynamics claims (C111-C113), marked UNCERTAIN due to limited video observations without systematic quantification. No corresponding peer review evaluation found explicitly addressing valve opening/closing dynamics.
